idiom_name: scalatestplus-selenium Page trait + ScalaTest Selenium DSL (go to, clickOn)
implementation_notes: ScalaTest's Selenium integration provides the pattern's Scala home: mix the Page trait into a page class (it supplies the url member for the `go to myPage` navigation form), drive elements through the DSL's implicit browser (textField, pwdField, emailField, textArea, clickOn), and keep the class's methods as the page's services. What replaces the classic structure is the trait plus the DSL's type-directed element lookup; plain Scala classes over WebDriver also work, but the DSL is the idiomatic route. Since ScalaTest 3.1 the integration lives in a separate artifact (org.scalatestplus selenium), so the dependency is explicit.
pitfalls: The DSL's implicit browser is created per test thread; a page object that captures it in a field, or is shared across parallel suites, breaks.
The Page trait only standardises the URL for `go to`: load verification and element re-resolution are still your code, so navigation methods must return the next page object themselves.
The Selenium DSL moved out of ScalaTest core into the scalatestplus-selenium artifact; code written against older versions that bundled it no longer compiles unchanged.
